title: WSPC Book Series in Unconventional Computing
why: A publisher's series page listing the handbook of unconventional computing and volumes on reversible cellular automata, actin computation, quantum computer music and arts and philosophy.

title: Metabiology and the complexity of natural evolution
why: An outreach article on Carsetti's view that natural computation is embodied and cannot be reduced to purely syntactic processing; a position, not a measurement.

title: Introducing Un-0: Generating Images with Coupled Oscillators
why: A start-up's post on a simulated oscillator network that generates images (FID 6.74 on ImageNet 64x64); no hardware energy measured. Weights and code released.

title: Extreme Event Likelihoods with Guided Generative Models
why: A vendor blog on guiding a diffusion climate emulator toward tropical cyclones to estimate odds ratios; an example of generative models as risk-analysis tools.

title: Making Unconventional Computing Practical
why: A practitioner's essay arguing that processing-in-memory, neuromorphic and thermodynamic chips reached customers by keeping one benefit and going digital. One author's view.

title: Could a computer scientist build a brain?
why: An essay reading evolution, development and learning as one process on different time scales, with the genome as a compressed record that development unfolds.

title: The Tacit Knowledge Series
why: A long-running series on knowledge that cannot be captured in words and how expertise is acquired.

title: Ingressing Minds: Causal, Non-Physical Patterns In-Form Natural, Synthetic, and Hybrid Embodiments
why: Michael Levin's theoretical paper proposing that mathematical patterns relate to physical objects as minds relate to bodies; a philosophical proposal, not an experiment.

title: The brain is not mental! coupling neuronal and immune cellular processing in human organisms
why: A Frontiers paper arguing that cognition is distributed across all the body's cells, not the brain alone; a theoretical argument.

title: Programmable Probabilistic Computer with 1,000,000 p-bits
why: Measured: a million probabilistic bits on 18 FPGAs sustaining 10^12 updates a second, checked against a GPU reference on spin-glass optimisation.

title: Bayesian inference with a polymer probabilistic computer
why: Four conjugated-polymer probabilistic bits sampling 16-state Bayesian posteriors within the spread expected of ideal bits.

title: Evaluating Positive Feedback Adiabatic Logic in 16nm FinFET with a Realistic Power-Clock
why: A simulation study of adiabatic logic at 16 nm finding energy advantages over static CMOS in small circuits, and three sources of loss that limit them.

title: Magic state cultivation on Willow
why: Google's account of a roughly 40-fold error reduction for magic states and 99.99% logical T-state fidelity on its Willow chip, published in Science.

title: IBM Quantum Open Plan updates
why: Describes free access to real quantum hardware (10 minutes per 28 days) for outsiders.

title: THRML
why: Open-source JAX library for blocked Gibbs sampling and energy-based models, from Extropic.
